title: Effects of different ventilation strategies on right ventricular function
summary:
Patients in the intensive care unit frequently require mechanical ventilation. Mechanical ventilation can also place strain on the heart; however, its effects on cardiac function are difficult to assess in routine clinical practice. Such assessment would be important for optimizing ventilator settings. This is particularly relevant in patients with severe acute respiratory failure, in whom the right ventricle is already under increased strain due to the underlying disease and may be further affected by mechanical ventilation.

This study will be conducted during routine intensive care treatment in patients with severe acute respiratory failure, with and without extracorporeal lung support (ECMO), who require a clinically indicated computed tomography (CT) scan of the lungs. Cardiac function will be assessed using ultrasound (echocardiography), and lung function will be evaluated using electrical impedance measurements. These assessments will be repeated after a short interval with modified ventilator settings and compared with the findings from CT imaging.

The aim of the study is, first, to quantify right ventricular dimensions using three-dimensional echocardiography and to validate these measurements by comparison with CT imaging. Second, the study seeks to evaluate the impact of mechanical ventilation on the right ventricle by assessing changes in its volume.

interventions.name: A total of 47 mechanically ventilated patients will be included. In all cases, a clinically indicated computed tomography (CT) scan of the thorax has been performed in accordance with the standard procedures of the Department of Anesthesiology and Operative Intensive Care Medicine and the Department

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Written informed consent provided by the patient or their legal representative
Analgosedated patients receiving mechanical ventilation
Presence of a central venous catheter and an arterial catheter
Hemodynamic stability under intensive care treatment (mean arterial pressure ≥ 65 mmHg, cardiac output ≥ 4.5 L/min/m² body surface area)
Clinically indicated requirement for computed tomography of the thorax
Exclusion criteria:
Congenital cardiac malformations, severe valvular dysfunction, or severe arrhythmias
Life expectancy of less than 24 hours
Prior surgical interventions involving the organs under investigation
